subject: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency & throughput next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Zhang <oliver@finpay.com>, Sara Kim <sara.kim@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency & throughput next steps

Hi Oliver / Sara — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and clear next steps so we don’t lose momentum.

Recap
- Primary objective: production-grade conversational assistant for FinPay payments flows (auth, reconciliation, fraud triage).
- Performance targets you called out: p95 latency goal ~200ms, p99 <600ms under realistic peak traffic.
- Estimated peak concurrency from your side: ~300 QPS during morning batch windows; typical steady state ~50–80 QPS.
- Data & compliance: PCI-adjacent product (no card data sent), but you need VPC peering + SOC2 evidence for enterprise procurement.

Immediate recommendation (from our side)
- Given the p95/p99 targets at ~300 QPS peak, Dedicated capacity is the safest option for predictable latency and isolation. Hosted API can work for early experimentation but will require aggressive caching and will likely see more variance at the p99 tail.
- Suggested approach: short Dedicated PO (2–4 GPUs reserved) for a 2-week pilot + capacity-sizing call to confirm instance class and autoscale policy. We’ll run a validation load test to demonstrate p95/p99 numbers.

Next steps
1) I’ll attach our Dedicated pricing & SLA doc for a baseline (attached).
2) Can we schedule a 30–45 min capacity sizing call early next week with your infra lead to walk through request profile and telemetry exports?
3) If you’re comfortable, we’ll stand up a 2-week pilot on Dedicated and run a joint load validation. If ETA/ops require, we can do a smaller Hosted trial in parallel for feature validation.

Questions for you (short)
- Confirm: are the p95/p99 targets above accurate? Any tighter SLOs for specific endpoints?
- Do you have a preferred start date for a pilot (week of Jun 28 or Jul 5)?

Attachments: SLA_dedicated_pricing.pdf (pdf), dedicated-architecture-diagram.png (image)

Thanks — I’ll loop Marissa in on pricing & SOW draft.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Oliver Zhang <oliver@finpay.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Kim <sara.kim@finpay.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency & throughput next steps

Dylan — thanks for the clear summary. Notes/answers below.

- Targets: p95 <200ms and p99 <600ms are correct for the user-facing payment flows. For internal async jobs (batch reconciliation) we can tolerate higher latency.
- Traffic: current day-to-day is ~60 QPS, with peak windows up to ~320 QPS (10–12am EST spike). Monthly request volume ~12M API calls.
- Compliance: we will need SOC2 + IP allowlist/VPC peering. SOC2 report should be recent (within 12 months).

Yes — based on what you described we are leaning Dedicated as well. A few asks before we commit to the pilot:
1) Can you share a short expected sizing recommendation (GPU class + estimated reserved count) based on the 320 QPS peak?
2) Ballpark pilot cost for a 2-week Dedicated test (include reserved base + overage).
3) Any SLA exceptions or mitigation if p99 spikes during pilot?

We’re available for the sizing call next Tue (Jun 29) 10–11am EST or Thu (Jul 1) 9–10am EST. Either works for our infra lead.

Thanks — Oliver
Oliver Zhang
Head of Platform Engineering | FinPay
oliver@finpay.com

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Zhang <oliver@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sara Kim <sara.kim@finpay.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency & throughput next steps

Oliver — great, thanks for confirming. Short answers and proposed next steps below.

Sizing (preliminary)
- For conversational generation (2–3k tokens per request median) and target p99 <600ms at 320 QPS: estimate 4 x A100-style GPUs with Dedicated pool + autoscale buffer. Exact SKU depends on model size (we’ll confirm on the sizing call).

Pilot cost (2 weeks, ballpark)
- Reserved baseline (4 GPUs): ~$18K for 2 weeks (includes dedicated pool + monitoring + SOC2 evidence bundle).
- Overage / burst: hourly burst capacity available at metered rate; we’ll include an explicit cap in the pilot SOW.

SLA & mitigation during pilot
- During pilot we operate with a pilot SLA (no enterprise credits), but we’ll commit to run joint load tests and share real telemetry. If p99 breaches are observed we’ll: (a) adjust batching/kv-cache tuning, (b) scale up the pool for the test window, and (c) document fixes and recommended final sizing.

Next steps
1) Marissa will send a draft SOW + pilot pricing worksheet today.
2) Confirm sizing call: we’ll take Tue Jun 29 10:00am EST. Please add your infra lead (invite to follow).
3) We’ll provision the pilot environment after signed pilot SOW and a short PO (procurement usually handles).

If you want a Hosted parallel trial (feature validation only) we can standby a small Hosted key — but agree Dedicated is the right path for latency/throughput.

I’ll attach the pricing PDF and architecture diagram again for reference.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Office: +1 (415) 555-0132
